chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no objection to scattering walnuts and sugar.'

Thus, it does not contradict the first two narrations, because what this narration encompasses is the permissibility of scattering, and it does not state that it is permissible to take what was scattered and plunder it. The first two narrations contain the dislike of that (plundering), and there is no contradiction between them in any case.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to scatter food items like nuts and sugar in public, and can others take them?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *nathr* (scattering goods like walnuts or sugar in public spaces), distinguishing between the permissibility of the act itself and the right of others to take them. Shaykh al-Tusi explains that this does not contradict other hadiths expressing *karahiya* (dislike) of plundering (*nahb*) because the permission to scatter does not imply a waiver of ownership rights, thus reconciling the texts within Shia jurisprudence.
